# dlaed6

> Computes the positive or negative root (closest to the origin) of the secular equation.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaed6 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlaed6';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaed6( kniter, orgati, rho, d, strideD, z, strideZ, finit, tau ) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `kniter` | `integer` | Iteration count hint from dlaed4 |
| `orgati` | `boolean` | If true, root is between `d[1]` and `d[2]`; otherwise between `d[0]` and `d[1]` |
| `rho` | `number` | Scalar in the secular equation |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 3</sub> | Input array of length 3 containing the original eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| `z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 3</sub> | Input array of length 3 containing the updating vector components |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `z` |
| `finit` | `number` | Value of f at 0 |
| `tau` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output array of length 1; `tau[0]` receives the computed root |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `kniter`: Refer to DLAED4 for its significance.
- `orgati`: If `ORGATI` is true, the needed root is between d(2) and d(3); otherwise it is between d(1) and d(2). See DLAED4 for further details.
- `rho`: Refer to the equation f(x) above.
- `d`: D satisfies $d(1) < d(2) < d(3)$.
- `z`: Each of the elements in z must be positive.
- `finit`: The value of f at 0. It is more accurate than the one evaluated inside this routine (if someone wants to do so).
- `tau`: The root of the equation f(x).

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success, 1 if convergence fails

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaed6.ndarray(
    kniter, orgati, rho,
    d, strideD, offsetD,
    z, strideZ, offsetZ,
    finit,
    tau
) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `kniter` | `integer` | Iteration count hint from dlaed4 |
| `orgati` | `boolean` | If true, root is between `d[1]` and `d[2]`; otherwise between `d[0]` and `d[1]` |
| `rho` | `number` | Scalar in the secular equation |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 3</sub> | Input array of length 3 containing the original eigenvalues |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `z` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 3</sub> | Input array of length 3 containing the updating vector components |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `z` |
| `finit` | `number` | Value of f at 0 |
| `tau` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output array of length 1; `tau[0]` receives the computed root |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `kniter`: Refer to DLAED4 for its significance.
- `orgati`: If `ORGATI` is true, the needed root is between d(2) and d(3); otherwise it is between d(1) and d(2). See DLAED4 for further details.
- `rho`: Refer to the equation f(x) above.
- `d`: D satisfies $d(1) < d(2) < d(3)$.
- `z`: Each of the elements in z must be positive.
- `finit`: The value of f at 0. It is more accurate than the one evaluated inside this routine (if someone wants to do so).
- `tau`: The root of the equation f(x).

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success, 1 if convergence fails

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = 1`, failure to converge

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlaed6 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlaed6';

const d = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 3.0, 7.0 ] );
const z = new Float64Array( [ 0.3, 0.5, 0.8 ] );
const tau = new Float64Array( 1 );
const rho = 0.5;
const finit = rho + (z[0]/d[0]) + (z[1]/d[1]) + (z[2]/d[2]);

const info = dlaed6( 2, true, rho, d, 1, z, 1, finit, tau );
console.log( 'info:', info, 'tau:', tau[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAED6`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLAED6 computes the positive or negative root (closest to the origin) of

```text
                 z(1)        z(2)        z(3)
f(x) =   rho + --------- + ---------- + ---------
                d(1)-x      d(2)-x      d(3)-x
```

It is assumed that

if `ORGATI` = .true. the root is between d(2) and d(3); otherwise it is between d(1) and d(2)

This routine will be called by DLAED4 when necessary. In most cases, the root sought is the smallest in magnitude, though it might not be in some extremely rare situations.

### Further Details

10/02/03: This version has a few statements commented out for thread safety (machine parameters are computed on each entry). SJH.

05/10/06: Modified from a new version of Ren-Cang Li, use

Gragg-Thornton-Warner cubic convergent scheme for better stability.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
